new.n: 'Battle-Axe' railroad grade (Washburn, Bayfield & Iron River RR), near Iron River
new.pl: Straight SW-NE grade through secs. 16/21, 15, 11 and 2 of T47N R9W, crossing the Northern Pacific in sec. 11, on the line from Iron River toward Washburn
new.v: Spikes, tie plates, rail hardware, lost coins and tools along the grade
new.st: Burnham (1929): the Battleaxe railroad was 'abandoned except for 9 miles into Iron River, then gone'. The Washburn Times (1 May 1902, p1) shows that the 'Battle-Axe' was the Washburn, Bayfield & Iron River Railroad, then in receivership: the Northern Pacific offered to buy it, and Washburn citizens agreed to secure a 100-ft right of way 'on the main line of said road... between the villages of Washburn and Iron River'. A Superior Evening Telegram item (6 Jul 1907, p10) shows it still running in 1907. The c.1915 Hixson plat of the Town of Iron River and the 1938 aerial show a straight SW-NE corridor here running toward Washburn; the pin is on that line, good to about 1 km.
new.t: Look on LiDAR for the raised grade and cuts along the SW-NE line; ask before entering private land.
